Harris, restaurateur and author Alexander Smalls, and cultural icon Big Freedia explore how food serves as a powerful expression of identity, heritage, community, and culture in one of America's most beloved culinary destinations.

More than a conversation about what's on the plate, this session is a tribute to the culture, creativity, and community that make New Orleans the most delicious city on earth.

Title: How Community Investing Fuels Black Entrepreneurship
Description:
What if helping a Black-owned business grow cost less than dinner?

Too often, talented entrepreneurs are overlooked by traditional lenders and lack access to the family wealth networks that have helped many others launch and scale their businesses. This conversation explores how everyday people can help close that gap through community-powered investing.

Hear firsthand from founders who successfully raised capital through Kiva, learn how contributions as small as $25 can help fuel business growth, and discover how collective action can unlock opportunity in underserved communities. You'll leave inspired—and with a simple roadmap for putting your dollars to work in the businesses and communities you believe in.

Title: Travel Reimagined: Access, Ownership & Community
Description:
Travel is changing—but who is it really becoming more accessible for? This conversation explores how technology, community, and entrepreneurship are reshaping the travel experience for Black travelers. From AI tools that make planning more affordable and less overwhelming, to founders building culturally rooted travel brands that center overlooked communities, this session connects access with ownership.

Attendees will learn how innovation is lowering barriers to travel, why community relationships matter in creating meaningful and affordable experiences, and how Black founders are building businesses that reflect the way we want to explore the world.

Title: Automating the Hustle, Building What’s Yours
Description:
The future of work isn’t coming—it’s already here. As AI reshapes industries and traditional career paths become less predictable, many founders and professionals are asking the same question: What does stability look like now?

This panel explores how to move from overwork to ownership by leveraging AI, systems, and strategy. From turning your expertise into income streams to using AI as your “invisible intern,” this conversation is about reclaiming your time, protecting your energy, and building something that works for you.

Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how to navigate workforce shifts, use AI practically, and design a more sustainable path forward.

Title: Unemployed, Underpaid, Undervalued: The Real State of Black Women’s Work

We’ll unpack the structural issues driving unemployment and underemployment, while uplifting the strategies Black women are using to survive, resist, and reimagine the future of work.

Lyrics on Trial: The Battle for Free Expression in the Courtroom
Description: There is a growing and controversial practice of introducing rap lyrics and other creative works as evidence in criminal trials across the United States. Panelists will explore how this trend disproportionately impacts Black and Brown artists and hip-hop performers. This dynamic raises urgent questions about racial bias in the justice system and the erosion of First Amendment protections for artistic expression. The discussion will also consider the opposing viewpoint that creative works may, under certain circumstances, constitute legitimate and relevant evidence in a court of law. Drawing on legal, cultural, and social perspectives, panelists will explore solutions that safeguard artistic creativity and free expression while upholding the integrity of the criminal justice system.

Title: The Future of Work: Unlocking Apprenticeships and Alternative Career Pathways
Description:
As technology reshapes industries and employers increasingly prioritize skills over traditional credentials, new pathways to meaningful careers are emerging.  Apprenticeships, workforce training programs, industry certifications, and other alternative routes are creating opportunities for individuals to gain practical experience, earn while they learn, and access high demand careers without following a conventional four year degree path.
This panel will explore how businesses, educators, policymakers, and workforce leaders are reimagining talent development to meet the needs of a rapidly changing economy.

Title: Seats at the Table: Protecting Black Power After Callias
Description:
This panel gets real. We're pulling together lawyers, organizers, elected officials, economists, and movement leaders to talk about what Louisiana v. Callais means for Black America - and where we go from here. Not just politically. Culturally. Economically. All of it.
Black power has never lived in one place. It lives in the Black-owned business that's been anchoring the same block for thirty years. It lives in the music, the food, the language this whole country borrows from. It lives in wealth being built, protected, and handed down. Callais hits the ballot box - and the fight runs much deeper than that. This panel holds the whole thing. We'll get into proportional representation too-  what it actually means, why it matters for Black communities, and how it works as a real structural solution when maps get drawn to dilute Black voting power.
